ip_top_stories.title: Authors Sue Meta's AI Scientists Directly in Llama Copyright Case
ip_top_stories.summary: Authors have taken the unusual step of suing Meta's AI scientists personally in the ongoing Llama copyright litigation, escalating the legal strategy beyond targeting the company itself. The move signals an aggressive new tactic in AI copyright enforcement. The case centres on claims that Meta's Llama model was trained on copyrighted works without authorisation.

ip_top_stories.title: UMG and Sony seek to add over 61k recordings to Suno lawsuit after discovery reveals AI trained on 'millions' of their copyrighted tracks
ip_top_stories.summary: Universal Music Group and Sony Music are seeking to dramatically expand their lawsuit against AI music generator Suno, after discovery proceedings allegedly revealed the AI was trained on millions of their copyrighted recordings. The labels now want to add over 61,000 tracks to the complaint. The development significantly widens the scope of one of the music industry's most closely watched AI copyright cases.

ip_top_stories.title: Sony Music Files to Expand Udio Suit, Alleges 30K Infringed Works
ip_top_stories.summary: Sony Music has filed to expand its copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Udio, now alleging infringement across approximately 30,000 works. The expansion follows a pattern of major labels broadening their legal actions against AI music platforms as discovery uncovers the scale of training data use.

ip_top_stories.title: MiniMax loses bid to dismiss Disney copyright lawsuit over AI system
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has rejected Chinese AI firm MiniMax's attempt to have Disney's copyright lawsuit dismissed, allowing the case to proceed. Disney alleges MiniMax's AI system was trained on or used copyrighted Disney content without authorisation. The ruling keeps alive a significant cross-border AI copyright dispute.

ip_top_stories.title: Eisner Awards to Implement AI Policy Following Controversy
ip_top_stories.summary: The Eisner Awards has announced it will implement an AI policy after a controversy surrounding the Stardust anthology, which was withdrawn from consideration following concerns about AI-generated content. The move reflects growing pressure on publishing and creative awards bodies to address AI disclosure and eligibility standards. [Metered]

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI Must Produce Testimony From Musk Case in Copyright Suits
ip_further_links.summary: A court has ordered OpenAI to produce testimony from the Elon Musk litigation for use in separate copyright infringement suits against the company.

ip_further_links.title: Artist Sues Copyright Office Over its Refusal to Register His AI-Enhanced Photo
ip_further_links.summary: An artist has filed a lawsuit against the US Copyright Office after it declined to register an AI-enhanced photograph, directly challenging the Office's policy on AI-generated and AI-assisted works.

ip_further_links.title: Can you own a voice? Taylor Swift's latest legal move raises big questions for AI and copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Taylor Swift's legal action over her voice raises broader questions about whether AI-generated vocal likenesses can be protected under existing copyright and trademark law.

ip_further_links.title: Mind the Gap: States Step in to Address Ownership of AI-Generated Works Amid Federal Uncertainty
ip_further_links.summary: US states are beginning to legislate on AI-generated works ownership as Congress and federal agencies remain slow to provide clarity on copyright protection for AI outputs.

ip_further_links.title: Japan eyes rules to regulate AI summaries' 'free riding' on news
ip_further_links.summary: Japan is considering regulatory measures to prevent AI services from using news content without compensation, targeting the practice of AI summarisation of journalistic work.

ip_further_links.title: EU Call for Evidence Targets Generative AI's Impact on Copyright
ip_further_links.summary: The EU has launched a call for evidence examining generative AI's impact on copyright, as part of ongoing efforts to align AI regulation with existing intellectual property frameworks.

ip_further_links.title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence: the divergence of the EU and UK
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of how EU and UK copyright frameworks are diverging in their approach to AI training and text and data mining exceptions following Brexit.

ip_further_links.title: Legal Risk Could Deflate the GenAI Bubble
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis argues that mounting copyright litigation and unresolved IP liability pose a systemic legal risk that could significantly slow generative AI investment and development.

ip_further_links.title: The User Has Changed. Has Scholarly Publishing?
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how AI is transforming research workflows and asks whether academic publishing models are keeping pace with the changed needs and behaviours of users.

ip_further_links.title: Australian creatives urge the government to 'hold the line' on AI and copyright law
ip_further_links.summary: Australian creative industry groups are lobbying the government to resist pressure to weaken copyright protections in the face of AI industry lobbying, echoing similar campaigns in the UK and EU.
